cohort: 404 women in the gynecology and obstetrics clinic of a university hospital
finding: While there was no overall difference in birth satisfaction between women who had vaginal births and those who had cesarean births, specific aspects of satisfaction differed, and factors like desire for pregnancy, induction, planned birth method, and anesthesia type significantly influenced birth satisfaction.
mod_finding: Women who had normal birth had higher satisfaction from the healthcare team and respect for privacy, while those who had cesarean birth were more satisfied with comforting and hospital room.
